question: In which border areas did India and China agree on patrolling arrangements along the Line of Actual Control on 21 October 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Depsang and Demchok**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Line of Actual Control (LAC)** is the demarcation line that separates Indian and Chinese territories. It is not an internationally agreed boundary but a result of historical disputes.
 
• On **21 October 2024**, India and China reached an agreement on patrolling arrangements for specific border areas to reduce tensions and ensure peace. These areas included **Depsang and Demchok.**
 
• **Depsang** is a region located in the northern part of Ladakh, adjacent to Aksai Chin. It has been a site of repeated military standoffs between India and China. The agreement aimed to de-escalate tensions in this highly sensitive area.
 
• **Demchok** is situated in southeastern Ladakh and has been a contested area due to its proximity to Chinese-controlled territories. Frequent patrol encounters have occurred here, making it crucial for both nations to establish clear patrolling protocols.
 
• The agreement between the two nations is part of ongoing diplomatic efforts to resolve border disputes and ensure peace along the LAC. *Hence, the correct answer is Depsang and Demchok.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Line of Actual Control (LAC):**

 
 
• The **LAC** is approximately **3,488 kilometers long** and traverses several regions, including Ladakh, Uttarakhand, Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, and Arunachal Pradesh.
 
• It is divided into three sectors: the **Western Sector (Ladakh), Central Sector (Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh), and Eastern Sector (Arunachal Pradesh).**
 
• The LAC is not a mutually agreed boundary but rather a result of differing perceptions of territorial claims by India and China.
 
 
 
• **Depsang Region:**
 
 
• **Depsang Plains** are strategically important due to their proximity to the **Daulat Beg Oldie airstrip** and other critical military installations.
 
• The region has witnessed standoffs, particularly during the **2020 Galwan Valley clash**, highlighting its significance in India-China relations.
 
 
 
• **Demchok Region:**
 
 
• **Demchok** is located in southeastern Ladakh and is claimed by China as part of Tibet.
 
• The area is known for its strategic location and frequent military patrolling by both nations.
 
 
 
• **India-China Border Disputes:**
 
 
• India and China have long-standing territorial disputes, primarily over **Aksai Chin** and **Arunachal Pradesh.**
 
• Efforts to resolve these disputes have included agreements such as the **1993 Border Peace and Tranquility Agreement** and the **2005 Protocol on Modalities for the Implementation of Confidence-Building Measures.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Recent Developments in India-China Relations:**

 
 
• The **Galwan Valley clash in June 2020** marked a significant escalation in tensions, leading to enhanced military deployment along the LAC.
 
• Both nations have conducted **diplomatic talks** and **military-level discussions** to reduce tensions, with limited success in certain areas like Depsang and Demchok.
 
 
 
• **Strategic Importance of Ladakh:**
 
 
• **Ladakh** serves as a critical area for maintaining territorial integrity due to its proximity to sensitive regions like **Aksai Chin** and **Tibet.**
 
• The region also holds strategic importance in terms of **military logistics, connectivity, and surveillance operations.**
